EARF Globe
EARF · Round 27 · the globe

The acrylic globe is the mark; the idents are parked

Round 27, the owner: “Let’s go with the acrylic globe and have a color version, a black version, and a white version, and a version for each speaker”, and then: “I like discs for monochrome and acrylic for multicolor”. So the mark is the acrylic in colour and the seamed discs in black, in white and in each speaker’s colour; the set is in brand/mark/ and on the mark’s own page. The rails below draw every style in every rail, for reference. The idents and the Planet are parked, as the owner chose: their code stays in earth.py and their videos in brand/, but this page no longer plays them. What follows is the globe as round 25 and 26 left it.

The globe as a Death Star — its dish a driver

The outside is the Earth (round 25): the continents in green on the blue sea, coarse and rounded, the Americas facing you, the land kept clear of the dish and no specks. In the North Atlantic a dish that is a driver seen from the front: the surround red, the cone orange, the dust cap yellow, as the Earth’s core. It is 21° across, as in round 24b, with a deeper bowl, so its rings sit toward the middle: 24° was tried and pressed on every coast. Below 49 px a mid cut keeps only the two Americas, and at 24 px and under the small cut has no land and a 24° dish. In one colour it is knock-outs: the disc solid, the land, the surround and the dust cap knocked out to the ground. On each beat the cone pushes out, rebounds and settles, and a ring of sound, knocked out of the globe, crosses the Earth (parked in round 27). As an ident, the Planet (round 26, drawn as early Disney would have, parked in round 27): a star twinkles, the meteor grows out of it, draws back and falls on an arc, stretching, and splats on the North Atlantic; the Earth squashes and springs back, a shock runs over it and the sea ripples; a white cloud pops up puff by puff, chars black from the middle out and is eaten away into curling crescents, and the crater springs open, the meteor dropping into its core as the violet cap.

Theme — Atmosphere, with an icon for each speaker from the marks’ own circles, bars and triangles

Each icon is made as the cloud mark is: a few circles, bars and triangles, all filled, then every outline drawn over them, like stacked clear acrylic. Poison is two crossing bars with circles at the ends; Acid is a circle with a triangle on top.

Notes

Why it reads as the Earth

  • The axis leans 23.4°, as the Earth's does and as a desk globe's stand holds it. It also tips 22° toward you, so the parallels open into ovals and the far halves show behind the near ones.
  • The colours (round 25): blue and green lead, as the Earth's sea and land. The meridian facing you, the largest disc, is Poison green; the equator, the widest band, is Ice blue; north Flare red and south Acid yellow; of the side meridians, the one that shows more is Dust orange and the one that shows less Haze violet. Round 24 had violet facing you and the primaries on the parallels.
  • Discs in colour are flush (round 24b): no seams, no outline, no light. The globe is its six discs alone (round 25): no fill completes the circle where no disc reaches the rim, so its outline is the discs' own, the green disc's oval with the others' tips reaching past it. The strokes belong to the one-colour versions: there the seams are gaps in the ground, and the outline stays whole.
  • Acrylic (round 25) is the discs themselves, see-through, stacked as tinted sheets, each disc a slab a twentieth of the radius thick, its side, where it faces you, a deeper tone of its tint, as a polished acrylic edge looks. The green meridian facing you is the backing, as in the discs. One disc in front shows its own flat colour; where two cross they make one colour darker than either, whichever is in front, as two filters do: red over violet crimson, blue over violet indigo, and the opposite pairs smoky, blue over orange taupe and yellow over violet brown. Where no disc lies in front, the rings' far halves show through the green a little deeper than it, so each ring closes. Where a disc is, the ground takes nothing, so paper and ink match. Stacked in OKLab (a and b averaged, the lightness the darkest sheet's and lower for each sheet more and the less their hues agree); drawn per pixel on the graphics card (without WebGL, the flush discs). No edges (a cage of hoops, the critic found). In one colour (round 27) it keeps the ball: in black or white the discs cancel where they cross, as two films do in one ink, so every crossing shows without a tint; in a speaker's own colour the discs are stacked sheets of that speaker's acrylic held up to the light, lighter at the rim, deeper where more cross.
  • Lines are even, every line one weight, the far halves under the near. Round 22's lighter far halves (in brand/earth-lines-*.svg) remain for one colour at small sizes, where even lines tangle.
  • Seen from above the pole, the same rings are a speaker: rings round one centre, with the meridians as spokes. Round 23’s Kick used that view; round 24b makes the speaker a Death Star’s dish instead.
  • Round 23's tubes, the printer and the kick, and round 24's lit sphere and cut-open globe, are set aside; the first three stay in earth.py and in round 23's files.

The rails

  • The mark (round 27, the owner: "Let's go with the acrylic globe", then "I like discs for monochrome and acrylic for multicolor"): the acrylic in colour; the seamed discs in black, in white and in each speaker's colour, flat, as files in brand/mark/. The acrylic's own one-colour forms (the overlap cut and the tints) and the lines stay below, for reference.
  • Black only: paper, print, embossing and a one-colour etch. White only: dark grounds, and the etched mark on the acrylic.
  • One colour: each speaker's own mark, for the speaker, its box and its page. Avoid Acid on paper, where yellow is too faint; use it on ink.
  • Multicolour: the brand at large. Animated: screens only (the idents, the loader, the cursor).
  • Discs, flush, for colour. In one colour, the seamed discs or the even lines; below about 32 px round 22's lighter far halves read better.
  • Clear space: a quarter of the globe's width on every side. In the lockup, the globe is one and a half cap heights tall, centred on the letters.

The icons

  • Each works in the same rails as the globe: tinted, lines and black only. Fog's tint is nearly white, so on paper its outline carries it.
  • Where they could go: beside the mark on the speaker (etched as the mark is), on the end of the box, and as each speaker's tab on the site.
  • The names don't have to change to use them. Under Elements the icons read as hazard signs; under Clouds or Atmosphere, as weather.
